title: Bridge lead pocket notes and status templates
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a compact, on-call friendly runbook for the Bridge Lead role: quick triage signals, escalation levers, concise internal war-room checklist, and ready-to-send public/customer messaging. Treat as a pocket guide — more detailed playbooks (capacity, routing fallbacks) live in Confluence (CONF-3482).

Status: draft — intended for trial with next two major incident responses, will iterate post-retro.

Quick TL;DR (one-liner):
- When paging occurs: ack, confirm incident id, assemble core roles (SE, SRE, NetEng, PM), post initial status to status page and #ops-incident, and schedule 15-min cadence.

Bridge Lead responsibilities (quick):
- Own the incident timeline and public messaging cadence.
- Decide when to escalate to Execs / Customer Success.
- Approve customer-facing templates and send or coordinate send.
- Call end-of-incident and coordinate next steps / follow-up.

Who to call (primary + backup):
- Service Eng (primary): oncall-service-eng@redwood, backup: @Asha_K
- SRE oncall (primary): @oncall-sre (PagerDuty), backup: @Jonah_P
- Net/Infra: @infrastructure, backup: @Elena_G
- Customer Success lead for affected account(s): contact via CS Pager and Slack channel #cs-incident

Immediate war-room checklist (first 0-10 minutes):
1) Acknowledge on PagerDuty, create INC-XXXXX if not auto-created.
2) Post to #ops-incident with one-line and playbook header (see Slack templates below).
3) Confirm blast radius: which customers, regions, models affected (list precise model IDs if applicable).
4) Gather metrics: error rate, latency distribution, affected hosts/pods, recent deploys/rollouts.
5) If customer-visible, set status page to "investigating" (template 1).
6) Start a shared doc (this file + incident notes) and capture timeline entries (timestamp + actor + action).
7) Decide SLO/priority and whether to call in extra support (DBA/hardware).

Internal cadence & timing (recommended):
- 0 min: initial ack + investigating post
- 10 min: first internal triage update
- 30 min: decision point (workaround vs escalation) & customer comm if needed
- every 30 min thereafter: public update or as major changes occur
- resolution: final post + RCA owner assigned within 48 hours

Escalation triggers (examples):
- Partial or full outage impacting >5% of requests or >3 enterprise customers
- Data loss or potential customer data exposure
- Degradation that persists >30 minutes despite mitigation attempts

Short technical triage checklist (for SRE/Eng leads):
- Check recent deploys / rollouts (k8s rollout history, CI pipelines)
- Inspect svc metrics: 5xx rate, 4xx spikes, latency P95/P99, queue lengths
- Evaluate autoscale events and node health (OOMs, GPU errors)
- Check KV cache and prefix cache hits; look for cache evictions
- Reproduce minimal failing call from a safe test environment

Status page templates (copy/paste friendly)
- INITIAL (Investigation):
  Title: Partial service disruption for [SERVICE_NAME]
  Body: We are investigating reports of increased errors and latency for [SERVICE_NAME] beginning at [TIME UTC]. Some customers in [REGION] may experience failures for model inference and embedding requests. Our engineers are actively investigating. We will provide another update by [ETA_T+30min].
  Impact: Intermittent failures / degraded performance for a subset of requests
  Mitigation: Engineers are triaging and collecting logs.

- UPDATE (Mitigation in progress):
  Title: Ongoing mitigation for [SERVICE_NAME]
  Body: Engineers have identified [brief cause or suspected subsystem] and are applying mitigations (rolling back recent deploys / scaling capacity / restarting affected hosts). Error rates have decreased by ~[X%] but some customers may still observe degraded responses. Next update by [ETA_T+30min].
  Impact: Reduced errors but intermittent failures remain
  Mitigation: Rolling remediation in progress; temporary routing fallback enabled for high-priority customers

- RESOLVED:
  Title: Incident resolved — [SERVICE_NAME]
  Body: We resolved the issue affecting [SERVICE_NAME] at [TIME UTC]. Service performance has returned to normal and error rates are at expected baselines. We will follow up with a post-incident review and action items. If you continue to experience problems, contact support@redwood.com and reference incident [INC-XXXXX].
  Impact: Service restored
  Mitigation: Permanent fix and RCA will be published in the postmortem

Customer email templates
- Short (high-trust, human):
  Subject: Service disruption update — [SERVICE_NAME]
  Hi [CustomerName],

  We’re currently investigating an issue affecting [SERVICE_NAME] that may impact API responses. Our engineers are actively working on mitigation and we’ll follow up within 30 minutes with an update. We apologize for the disruption — we know this impacts your product.

  Best,
  Redwood Ops on behalf of the engineering team

- Detailed (when asked by CS/Account):
  Subject: Incident [INC-XXXXX] — technical update and interim mitigations
  Hi [CustomerName],

  Summary: Between [TIME_START] and [TIME_NOW] some inference calls to [SERVICE_NAME] returned errors (5xx) or experienced elevated latency. Impacted operations include [list].

  What we’re doing: Our team identified [suspected subsystem] and applied temporary mitigations (e.g., routing to warm pools, rollback of deployment abc, increasing autoscale limits). We are monitoring and expect continued improvements over the next [N] minutes.

  Next steps: Complete mitigation, validate recovery, publish RCA and timeline within 48 hours. We’ll keep you updated — please escalate to your CS lead if this is impacting production.

  Sincerely,
  [Bridge Lead name] on behalf of Redwood Engineering

Slack incident post templates (for #ops-incident)
- Initial (paste immediately):
  [INC-XXXXX] Investigating: elevated error rate for [SERVICE_NAME] in [REGION]. Affected: ~[X] hosts / [Y] customers. Bridge: @Riley_Chen. SRE oncall: @oncall-sre. Please join war-room: [link to doc].

- Update (copy each cadence):
  [INC-XXXXX] Update: mitigation started — rolling restart of pods in cluster [abc] at [TIME]. Error rate down [X%]. Next update in 30m.

- Resolved:
  [INC-XXXXX] Resolved at [TIME]. Root cause suspected: [brief]. Postmortem owner: @Jonah_P. RCA due: [DATE].

Internal war-room checklist (detailed items):
- Ensure recording of the session for exec review
- Assign scribe for minute-by-minute notes and actions, capture owner and ETA for each action
- Lock any public-facing deploys until stabilization confirmed
- Confirm CS/Account mapping and whether proactive customer outreach required
- If multi-region, confirm failover status for each region
- If stateful stores impacted, confirm backups and data integrity checks

Post-incident actions (short list):
- Assign RCA owner within 24 hours
- Publish interim timeline within 48 hours
- Track remediation tasks in a short-lived board (e.g., Jira label: inc-XXXXX-followup)
- Measure impact on cost/throughput for next 7 days (if mitigation used extra capacity)

Templates & copy reuse guidance:
- Keep public messaging concise and avoid hypothesizing root causes. Use phrases like "suspected subsystem" not "root cause" until RCA done.
- For customer emails, prefer the short template unless CS requests detailed technical update.

Notes to self / open questions (work-in-progress):
- Consider a "high-priority customer" tier on status page that shows dedicated messages to affected accounts (maybe a secure portal link?)
- Should the Bridge Lead be the one to hit the status page publish button or should CS lead? For now Bridge Lead owns it for speed.
- Need an integration test for the status page that ensures template renders properly with incident variables

Quick copy checklist before hitting send:
- Verify times are in UTC and clearly labeled
- Replace placeholders ([SERVICE_NAME], [REGION], [INC-XXXXX])
- Confirm owner and contact information present

Revision history / changelog (draft):
- 2024-11-02 initial pocket draft — Riley Chen
- 2024-11-15 added customer email templates and escalation triggers — Asha Kapoor
- 2024-11-20 tightened cadence recommendations and added short triage checklist — Jonah Patel

End notes:
This file is intentionally compact and pragmatic — keep it to one page in practice. Use this as the starting script for the first 60 minutes of an incident. Longer playbooks (DB incidents, data corruption, legal/PII) remain separate and referenced by this document.

Unresolved / future items to add:
- Pre-approved exec notification templates (legal + comms)
- Clear rules for when to patch notes to status page vs email vs CS direct outreach
- Checklist for degraded-but-not-outage (e.g., P50 shifted but SLO still met)

[END OF DRAFT - Bridge lead pocket notes]"
